body.statement: Let \(m=|\mathcal A|\), \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\), and \(n=|V|\). If the oracle-instance \(\mathsf X_{\mathrm{phys}}\) is feasible, then it has a lexicographically canonical accepting uniform certificate with at most \(k\) nonempty records, one owned transcript schema for each factor, no empty-ownership record, and no larger cost than any accepting acquired collection. Every transcript has at most \(n\) strict restrictions and at most \(8(n+1)^2\lceil\log_2(n+L+k+2)\rceil\) bits. Consequently \(N_E\le B_{\mathrm{cert}}=k(m+L+k+n(1+L))+8k(n+1)^2\lceil\log_2(n+L+k+2)\rceil\le8k(N_{\mathrm{in}}+1)^4\). Thus the lexicographically first optimum \(E^{\star}\) exists and its certificate length is polynomial in the structural input and \(k\); oracle replies are separately charged by \(N_{\mathcal O}\).
body.justification: The bound separates compact existential certificate data from potentially large, explicitly charged oracle support replies.
body.gap: Fixed-source completeness provides no canonical polynomial bound on an endogenous physical acquisition certificate or its transcript schema.
body.consumer: The exact optimizer can bound certificate enumeration while reporting source-interface cost separately.

obligation.what_is_open: The unresolved implication is that every feasible generic acquired collection is dominated in cost by a certificate with at most \(k\) nonempty records.
obligation.obstruction: That implication is exactly the unresolved uniform-source normal form. The fixed-label transcript bound alone controls the size of a chosen record but cannot supply a single record valid over every branch.
obligation.attempted: I derived the record-count, transcript encoding, polynomial bit bound, and lexicographic-minimum argument after conditioning on the uniform-source theorem; removing that condition would silently assume the crux.
obligation.partial_result:
Conditional on the uniform-source theorem, discard empty-ownership records and merge identical retained records.  There are then at most \(k\) records.  With \(n=|V|\), the explicit mask encoding from the transcript lemma can be padded to at most
\[
 8(n+1)^2\left\lceil\log_2(n+|\mathrm{LIT}|+k+2)\right\rceil
\]
bits per transcript.  Adding the fixed-width masks gives exactly the displayed \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\) upper bound.  The self-delimiting structural input explicitly lists every vertex, action, literal, and factor, so each of \(n,|\mathcal A|,|\mathrm{LIT}|,k\) is at most \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\); elementary domination then yields \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\le8k(N_{\mathrm{in}}+1)^4\).  Finiteness and exact rational costs give a lexicographically first minimum among the bounded certificates.  What is missing is the unconditional appeal to the unresolved uniform-source theorem needed to dominate every accepting generic acquisition \(E_0\).
